subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which process in the nitrogen cycle returns nitrogen gas to the atmosphere, reducing soil fertility?
questions.explain: Denitrifying bacteria in anaerobic soils convert nitrate back to nitrogen gas, lowering soil nitrogen.

questions.q: The clonal selection and activation of a specific B-cell typically requires:
options: Antigen binding plus stimulation by an activated T-helper cell releasing cytokines
Only the antigen binding to the B-cell receptor
questions.explain: Most B-cells require both antigen binding and signals (cytokines) from T-helper cells to divide and differentiate.

options: Favour the intermediate (mean) phenotype and reduce variation
Favour both extremes against the mean
questions.explain: Stabilising selection favours the mean phenotype, selecting against extremes and reducing variation.

questions.q: Courtship behaviour is important in evolution and classification because it:
options: Allows members of the same species to recognise each other and ensures reproductive isolation between species
questions.explain: Species-specific courtship allows recognition of conspecific mates and maintains reproductive isolation between species.

questions.q: Modern classification places organisms into three domains. These are:
questions.explain: The three-domain system divides life into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya based largely on rRNA sequence differences.

questions.q: In the carbon cycle, which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis fixes atmospheric CO2 into organic compounds, removing it from the air.

questions.q: Why is so little energy transferred between successive trophic levels?
options: Energy is lost through respiration, heat, and indigestible or uneaten material
Decomposers add energy at each level
All energy is converted to oxygen
questions.explain: Much energy is lost as heat in respiration and in material that is not eaten or not digested.

questions.q: Which sampling technique is most appropriate for estimating the population of a non-motile plant such as clover in a field?
questions.explain: Random quadrats are ideal for sessile organisms like plants, where individuals can be counted in a known area.

questions.q: Why are antibiotics ineffective against viral infections such as HIV?
options: Viruses lack the metabolic processes and structures (e.g. cell walls, ribosomes) that antibiotics target
Viruses are too large to be affected
questions.explain: Antibiotics target bacterial structures and processes; viruses use host-cell machinery and lack these targets, so antibiotics do not affect them.

questions.q: Sympatric speciation differs from allopatric speciation because it occurs:
options: Only after a geographical barrier forms
Without geographical separation, e.g. by behavioural or temporal isolation
questions.explain: Sympatric speciation happens within the same geographical area through reproductive isolation mechanisms other than geography.

questions.q: Self-antigens normally do not trigger an immune response because:
options: They are too small to be detected
Lymphocytes that would respond to the body's own antigens are destroyed or suppressed during development
questions.explain: During development, lymphocytes complementary to self-antigens undergo clonal deletion or suppression, preventing autoimmune attack.

questions.q: During primary succession, what is the key role of the pioneer species?
options: They form the stable climax community
They colonise bare rock and begin soil formation
They are the top predators of the food web
They prevent any further species from establishing
questions.explain: Pioneers such as lichens colonise inhospitable bare surfaces and start building soil for later species.
